svg.title: The same tool returning a formatted string and returning a dataclass
svg.desc: Two panels of equal size, each holding the same three stacked boxes at the same heights so only their contents differ. The left panel is tagged returns str: the function builds a formatted report, the published output schema wraps the whole thing in a single result field typed as a string, and what the model receives is one block of prose. Notes say the model has to read a number out of that prose, a client has nothing to validate against, and a renamed field is invisible. The right panel is tagged returns SystemSnapshot: the function returns a dataclass whose fields are annotated in the class body, the published output schema names every field and its type, and what the model receives is machine-readable JSON. Notes say the host can render a table, the client can validate the shape, a renamed field breaks loudly, and the text block still carries the same JSON. A closing line names a third outcome: a class whose attributes are assigned only inside its constructor publishes no output schema at all, with no warning, and ships the object representation as its text.
svg.text: The annotation is the only difference. Every box below it follows from that one line.
One string. To use a number the model has to read it out of
prose, and a client has nothing to validate against. Rename
a field and no consumer can tell.
Named, typed fields. The host can render a table, the client
can validate the shape, and a renamed field breaks loudly
instead of quietly. The text block still carries the JSON.
A class whose attributes are set only in __init__ takes a third path: outputSchema null, no warning, and the object repr as the text.
